_title: Percutaneous minimally invasive fusion/stabilization of the sacroiliac joint for the treatment of back pain

criteria.text: Percutaneous SIJ fusion is indicated for SIJ pain in patients who meet all 7 listed criteria
sub_conditions: Have undergone and failed a minimum 6 months of intensive non-operative treatment that must include medication optimization, activity modification, and active physical therapy
Patient’s report of non-radiating, unilateral pain that is caudal to the lumbar spine (L5 vertebrae), localized over the posterior SIJ, and consistent with SIJ pain

Localized tenderness with palpation of the posterior SIJ in the absence of tenderness of similar severity elsewhere (e.g. greater trochanter, lumbar spine, coccyx) and other obvious sources for their pain do not exist
Positive response to the thigh thrust test OR compression test AND 2 of the following additional provocative tests: Gaenslen’s test, Distraction test, Patrick’s sign
Absence of generalized pain behavior (e.g. somatoform disorder) or generalized pain disorders (e.g. fibromyalgia)

Imaging (plain radiographs and a CT or MRI) of the SI joint that excludes the presence of destructive lesions (e.g. tumor, infection) or inflammatory arthropathy that would not be properly addressed by percutaneous SIJ fusion
At least 75% reduction of pain for the expected duration of the anesthetic used following an image-guided, contrast-enhanced SIJ injection on 2 separate occasions
criteria.temporal: minimum 6 months of intensive non-operative treatment prior to consideration
criteria.source_span: Percutaneous minimally invasive fusion/stabilization of the sacroiliac joint (SIJ) for the treatment of back pain is indicated for the treatment of SIJ pain for patients with low back/buttock pain who meet all of the following criteria:

criteria.text: Diagnostic imaging must also rule out ipsilateral hip osteoarthritis and lumbar spine neural compression/degenerative condition
sub_conditions: Imaging of the ipsilateral hip (plain radiographs) to rule out osteoarthritis
Imaging of the lumbar spine (CT or MRI) to rule out neural compression or other degenerative condition that can be causing low back or buttock pain
criteria.source_span: Imaging of the ipsilateral hip (plain radiographs) to rule out osteoarthritis;

criteria.text: Percutaneous SIJ fusion is not indicated in the presence of any of the listed conditions
sub_conditions: Systemic arthropathy such as ankylosing spondylitis or rheumatoid arthritis
Generalized pain behavior (e.g. somatoform disorder) or generalized pain disorder (e.g. fibromyalgia)
Acute, traumatic instability of the SIJ
Neural compression as seen on an MRI or CT that correlates with the patient’s symptoms or other more likely source for their pain
